hard_constraints.translation: The agreement is between the County and the Bidder.
County offices are at 1 Harrison St. S.E., Leesburg, VA 20175.
County is seeking bids to construct the Ashburn Sheriff Station.
Bidder desires drawings for the sole purpose of responding to RFQ 205.
Purpose is to allow access to Confidential Information for the sole purpose of compiling/submitting a bid response.
Agreement is intended to ensure safety and security of the Ashburn Sheriff Station.
hard_constraints.reasoning: Stated as intent; slightly less than absolute factual necessity but clearly asserted.

hard_constraints.translation: Bidder will keep all Confidential Information in strict confidence.
hard_constraints.reasoning: Explicit commitment tied to signing; strong contractual language.

hard_constraints.translation: Bidder will only use Confidential Information on the Project.
Bidder warrants its employees/partners/subcontractors/agents/clients will be bound by confidentiality constraints.
Bidder shall not publish Confidential Information.
If Bidder is prohibited from publishing CI, then (expectedly) Bidder does not publish CI.
hard_constraints.reasoning: Contractual ‘shall not’ strongly implies intended compliance.

hard_constraints.translation: Bidder shall not make copies of Confidential Information.
If Bidder is prohibited from making copies, then (expectedly) Bidder does not make copies.
Bidder shall not retain copies of Confidential Information.
If Bidder is prohibited from retaining copies, then (expectedly) Bidder does not retain copies.
Bidder shall not disclose Confidential Information to any third party.
hard_constraints.reasoning: Explicit prohibition (‘shall not’), subject to carve-outs stated elsewhere.

hard_constraints.translation: If disclosure is necessary, then disclosure may be necessary.
If disclosure is required by judicial process, then disclosure is by judicial process.
hard_constraints.reasoning: ‘Required by judicial process’ semantically entails ‘by judicial process’.

hard_constraints.translation: Bidder will provide County notice of a request/demand to disclose Confidential Information.
All Confidential Information shall be destroyed within 10 days after award of the IFB.
All Confidential Information shall be destroyed within 10 days after completion of the IFB.
All Confidential Information shall be destroyed upon demand by the County.
Files containing Confidential Information shall be deleted from all Bidder web sites.
Files containing Confidential Information shall be deleted from all Bidder electronic devices.
Confidential Information includes photos, sketches, models, and drawings related to the project.
If CI includes those items, then those items are CI.
Bidder shall verify that downstream recipients destroyed Confidential Information.
Successful bidder shall destroy all Confidential Information within 10 days after final project completion.
Bidder agrees to indemnify and hold harmless the County for liabilities attributable to Bidder negligence related to CI.
Confidential Information shall be used in strict confidence solely for the allotted purpose.
Confidential Information means all information relating to design, layout, and operation of the Project.
If CI means all information relating to design/layout/operation, then related drawings/photos/etc. are CI.
hard_constraints.reasoning: Strong definitional/semantic inference; examples explicitly include these items.

hard_constraints.translation: If an exception applies (prior possession/public disclosure/independent development) or disclosure is necessary/required, then disclosure without prior written consent may be allowed.
hard_constraints.evidence: Section 4.A exceptions; Section 2 ‘may be necessary’ and ‘required by judicial process’
hard_constraints.reasoning: The text explicitly creates exceptions; modeling them as permission is strongly implied though not stated using the word ‘may’.

hard_constraints.translation: If the Bidder discloses CI without prior written consent, that disclosure should fall under an exception/necessity/judicial requirement.
hard_constraints.evidence: Section 4.A ‘without prior written consent … with the exception of the following’; Section 2 exceptions
hard_constraints.reasoning: Captures the intended structure of the carve-outs: disclosure without consent is only acceptable under exceptions.

hard_constraints.translation: If the Bidder discloses with prior written consent, then such disclosure is allowed.
hard_constraints.reasoning: Common-sense normative reading: consent implies permission.

hard_constraints.translation: Governing law shall be Virginia.
If the agreement shall be governed by Virginia law, then (expectedly) it is governed by Virginia law.
hard_constraints.reasoning: Strong contractual designation; treated as controlling.

hard_constraints.translation: If Virginia law governs, then it is not governed by Maryland, DC, or West Virginia law.
hard_constraints.evidence: Section 5 Governing Law (Virginia specified; alternatives added)
hard_constraints.reasoning: Mutual exclusivity of governing-law designations in ordinary legal interpretation.

hard_constraints.translation: Bidder waives objection to venue/jurisdiction of the Loudoun County Circuit Court.
Governing terms are limited to those contained in this Agreement.
Agreement is the complete integration of oral and written documents.
Agreement is the entire and final agreement between the parties.
Agreement may be amended only in a writing signed by authorized officials of both parties.
hard_constraints.reasoning: Explicit amendment condition (‘may be amended only in writing signed ...’).

hard_constraints.translation: If amendments are allowed only in signed writing, then (whenever amended) amendments are in signed writing.
hard_constraints.reasoning: Semantic tightening from ‘may be amended only ...’ to ‘is amended only ...’; not pure logic but strongly intended.

hard_constraints.translation: If the agreement is amended, it is amended only in writing signed by authorized officials of both parties.
hard_constraints.reasoning: Directly captures the ‘only in writing signed ...’ constraint as an implication from an amendment occurring.

hard_constraints.translation: Person signing will show title/authority to bind the firm.
Name and authorized signature must appear below.
If name/signature must appear below, then (expectedly) they appear below.
hard_constraints.reasoning: Strong expectation of satisfying a formal requirement.

hard_constraints.translation: If a general partner must sign for a limited partnership, then (expectedly) a general partner signs.
hard_constraints.evidence: Section 7 Authority to Bind (limited partnership rule)

hard_constraints.translation: If a manager must sign when specified by the articles, then (expectedly) the manager signs in that case.
hard_constraints.evidence: Section 7 Authority to Bind (LLC manager rule)

hard_constraints.translation: County requires a corporate authorization document be submitted with the proposal.

soft_constraints.translation: If the Bidder commits that it will keep CI in confidence, then (expectedly) it keeps CI in confidence.
soft_constraints.reasoning: ‘Will’ is a commitment; compliance is strongly expected but not logically guaranteed.

soft_constraints.translation: If Bidder commits it will only use CI on the Project, then (expectedly) Bidder only uses CI on the Project.
If Bidder warrants others will be bound, then (expectedly) they are bound.
soft_constraints.reasoning: A warranty is strong but actual binding may depend on external execution; still strongly implied.

soft_constraints.translation: If Bidder is prohibited from disclosing CI to third parties, then (expectedly) Bidder does not disclose CI to third parties.
soft_constraints.reasoning: Expected compliance, but carve-outs/real-world breach possibility reduce from 1.0.

soft_constraints.translation: Disclosure may be necessary to carry out duties under the agreement.
soft_constraints.reasoning: ‘May be necessary’ indicates possibility, not certainty.

soft_constraints.translation: Disclosure is required by judicial process in a legal proceeding (in some circumstances).
soft_constraints.reasoning: Stated as a conditional exception (‘to the extent ... required’); not always triggered.

soft_constraints.translation: If Bidder commits it will provide notice, then (expectedly) it provides notice.
If destruction within 10 days after award is required, then (expectedly) it is destroyed within that window.
soft_constraints.reasoning: Strong compliance expectation; not logical certainty.

soft_constraints.translation: If destruction within 10 days after IFB completion is required, then (expectedly) it is destroyed within that window.
If destruction upon demand is required, then (expectedly) it is destroyed upon demand.
If deletion from websites is required, then (expectedly) the files are deleted from websites.
If deletion from devices is required, then (expectedly) the files are deleted from devices.
If verification is required, then (expectedly) Bidder verifies destruction.
If the successful bidder is required to destroy CI after final completion, then (expectedly) it does so.
soft_constraints.reasoning: Expected compliance with a strict deadline.

soft_constraints.translation: If CI must be used in strict confidence solely for the purpose, then (expectedly) it is used that way.

If bidder waives objection to Loudoun County Circuit Court venue/jurisdiction, then venue/jurisdiction is not treated as being in alternative courts (e.g., Fairfax Circuit Court or federal district court).
soft_constraints.reasoning: The text designates Loudoun County Circuit Court; auxiliary negatives model typical mutually exclusive venue selections.

soft_constraints.translation: If the signer will show authority, then (expectedly) the signer shows authority.
If the County requires the authorization document, then (expectedly) it is submitted with the proposal.
soft_constraints.reasoning: Strong expectation of compliance, though submission is an action that could be violated.
